signals.notes: COMEX COPPER- #1, CFTC disaggregated FUTURES-ONLY basis (options excluded; NOT the futures-and-options combined report, which was not retrieved). Managed-money net long 78,648 lots (gross long 92,097 minus gross short 13,449); approx 892 kt at 25,000 lb = 11.33981 t per lot, conversion is mine. CROWDING IS MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED: percentile = count of weekly reports strictly below the current value divided by the total, over the 156 weekly COT reports dated on or after 2023-08-28 through 2026-08-18 (~3.0 years), same contract and same futures-only basis throughout; counts computed server-side by the CFTC API, not estimated. 154 of 156 below -> 98.7th percentile; z = (78,648 - 31,136) / 27,796 = +1.71 using the population sd over the same window (current observation included in the window). Window min -43,928, max +79,027; exactly ONE week in three years was higher and it was 2026-08-11, seven days earlier. Change: w/w -379 lots; 2-week +2,890; 12-month +53,039 (+207%) from +25,609 on 2025-08-19. MM net is 27.93% of open interest (281,563) versus 13.13% twelve months ago. DIRECTION SEMANTICS: bearish here means a mean-reversion and liquidation RISK TO THE EXISTING MOVE, not a bearish price call and not a short signal; a stretched position is a risk, not a direction on its own. THREE BINDING CAVEATS: (1) UNVINTAGED - retrieved live from the CFTC public API at decision time with no accepted connector vintage, so under MODULE_RULES 8A it cannot raise sufficiency or conviction and does NOT fill required row copper.managed-money-positioning; (2) STALE BY 10 DAYS - the 2026-08-25 report was not present on the API at retrieval, so this reading PREDATES the 2026-08-24 LME delivery squeeze and its 2026-08-25/26 relief entirely; (3) the profile requires 'a current COMEX COT observation' and this is not current, an independent second reason the row fails. Report integrity check passed: the five class nets sum to zero (+78,648 - 96,274 + 6,134 + 1,100 + 10,392 = 0) and both long and short legs reconcile to open interest 281,563 to the lot.

The gross-versus-net decomposition, emitted separately because a net level alone misreads what is driving the extreme. Managed-money GROSS SHORT 13,449 lots = 14.7th percentile (23 of 156 weekly reports below) of the same 156-week window; GROSS LONG 92,097 lots = 87.8th percentile (137 of 156 below); long:short ratio 6.85:1. ATTRIBUTION (MODULE_RULES 4a), an accounting IDENTITY, not an estimated sensitivity, so it carries no coefficient-basis risk: net 78,648 lots versus the 156-week mean net of 31,136 lots = an excess of +47,512 lots; long leg (92,097 - 69,671 mean long) = +22,426 lots, short leg (38,535 mean short - 13,449 actual) = +25,086 lots; 22,426 + 25,086 = 47,512 of the 47,512 observed -> 100% explained, 0% residual; 47.2% long accumulation, 52.8% short-side ABSENCE. READ: more than half the 98.7th-percentile net extreme is shorts who are not there rather than longs who piled in. Two consequences run in opposite directions and both are real - there is almost no short base left to squeeze (the fuel for a further leg up is largely spent), and there is nobody structurally obliged to buy a fall (an unwind is cleaner and faster). Direction is set bearish for the second effect only and the strength is deliberately low; this row SUPPORTS copper-managed-money-net-length-crowded and does not contradict it. Same unvintaged, ten-day-stale, futures-only limitations as that row.

THE RISK-PREMIUM LEG - the hedger side, reported because a managed-money-only read misses which way the physical trade leans. Producer/merchant/processor/user net -96,274 lots (gross long 28,940, gross short 125,214; approx -1.09 Mt net short, and 1.42 Mt gross short, conversions mine). Percentile on the SAME 156-week window and the same method as the managed-money row: only 13 of 156 weekly reports were more short -> 8.3rd percentile of net, i.e. roughly the 92nd percentile of SHORTNESS, against a window mean of -57,772 lots. LEAN: heavily short and PRESSING, not covering - the net short DOUBLED over twelve months (-47,555 on 2025-08-19 to -96,274 on 2026-08-18) while the price rose. Week-on-week they covered +1,243 lots (long -1,910, short -3,153), a rounding error against a 48,719-lot annual build and NOT a turn. Producer/merchant gross short is 44.47% of open interest, the single largest bucket in the whole report. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: whether hedgers are selling into a price they judge unsustainable or simply locking in a good year is a cost-curve question owned by commodity-cost-curve-fair-value, whose copper.cost-incentive-range row is unavailable - not proven from available data. Direction bearish reflects physical sellers pressing paper supply into the market, at low strength because the same fact is also what a physically tight market normally produces. Same unvintaged and ten-day-stale limitations.

WHO TOOK THE OTHER SIDE, as an exact identity. ATTRIBUTION (MODULE_RULES 4a), COMEX COPPER- #1 futures-only disaggregated basis, in LOTS: managed-money net length +53,039 lots over 12 months (+25,609 on 2025-08-19 to +78,648 on 2026-08-18) = producer/merchant net -48,719 lots (-47,555 to -96,274) absorbing 91.9%, plus swaps, other reportables and non-reportables combined -4,320 lots absorbing 8.1%, = -53,039 lots of the +53,039 lots observed -> 100% explained, 0% residual. Identity (the four class nets sum to zero by construction), NOT an estimated sensitivity. Supporting build: MM gross long +52,205 (+130.9%) while MM gross short was flat at -834 (-5.8%); total open interest +86,483 (+44.3%) from 195,080 to 281,563. Direction is NEUTRAL on purpose: this row states WHO is on each side, not which side is right. It is emitted separately from the two percentile rows because it is a 12-month FLOW decomposition, whereas those are LEVEL percentiles - the same underlying report, but different measured claims, and neither is a second vote for the other. Same unvintaged, ten-day-stale, futures-only limitations; both endpoint observations are from the same CFTC public API retrieval on 2026-08-28.

THE OPPOSING RISK, emitted as its own row and linked rather than averaged against the crowded-long row. Concentration is taken from the CFTC report's OWN PUBLISHED RATIOS; no holder identity is inferred anywhere, and no dealer gamma is inferred from option open interest (out of scope, forbidden). Largest 4 traders gross: 30.3% of OI SHORT versus 16.3% LONG. Largest 8 traders gross: 43.5% short versus 25.8% long. Largest 4 net: 28.2% short versus 15.7% long. Trader counts: 85 managed-money longs averaging 1,083 lots each versus 32 producer/merchant shorts averaging 3,913 lots each; 279 reporting traders in total. PERCENTILE, same 156-week window and method: top-4 gross short at 30.3% sits at the 79th percentile (124 of 156 weekly reports below); ties at exactly 30.3% are excluded from the 'below' count, so 79th is a LOWER BOUND on the rank. READ: liquidation risk is two-sided and the two sides are structurally different - a crowded but DISPERSED long book bleeds out on a fall with no short base obliged to buy it, while a smaller but far more CONCENTRATED short book is squeezable, which is the structure that produced the LME event of 2026-08-24 (cash-3M backwardation reported to approximately US$550/t, the highest in more than five years, before more than 20,000 t was delivered on 2026-08-25 and the spread collapsed to approximately US$248/t) [market-structure/99, unvintaged secondary, and that orb's formal delivery-pressure status is 'not assessable']. The contradicts link to copper-managed-money-net-length-crowded is DELIBERATE and correct: both risks are genuinely present, they point opposite ways, and under MODULE_RULES 8 this makes the futures-positioning cluster contradiction: true and never conviction-eligible. Same unvintaged and ten-day-stale limitations - and note this reading predates the squeeze it describes.

The one obtainable investor-FLOW direction, and it FADES the move rather than confirming it: LME investment funds / speculators cut net long copper positions by 6,340 lots to 53,914 lots, ending a two-week run of increases DESPITE higher prices, with the price within roughly 3% of a reported all-time high. Approximately 1.35 Mt at the standard 25-tonne LME copper lot - that conversion is INFERENCE, because the LME contract specification was not retrieved in this run. FOUR LIMITS, all material: (1) the source DOES NOT STATE THE COTR REPORT DATE, so this reading cannot be date-aligned with the 2026-08-18 COMEX print or with anything else, and the as_of above is the ARTICLE publication date, not the report date; (2) it is a broker comment piece summarising the COTR, i.e. unvintaged secondary, not the LME publication itself; (3) LME COTR and CFTC COT use DIFFERENT exchanges, different trader taxonomies and different report dates - they are NOT additive and NOT directly comparable, and no combined 'global spec length' figure is computed anywhere in this orb; (4) required row copper.lme-investment-fund-positioning demands >=3 years of LME investment-fund history, which DOES NOT EXIST in this run at all, so NO LME percentile or z-score is computable and none is printed - the row is marked unavailable, not substituted. The LME COTR is an entitled exchange publication with no lawful machine route reachable here and no licence was worked around.

EXPLICIT GAP ROW, emitted so the timing hole is machine-visible rather than buried in prose. Zero strength, neutral, non-voting. The most recent COT report available on the CFTC public API at retrieval on 2026-08-28 is dated 2026-08-18; the 2026-08-25 report was NOT present. The decision date is 2026-08-28, so EVERY positioning figure in this orb is TEN DAYS STALE, and it predates the LME delivery squeeze that peaked on 2026-08-24 and broke on 2026-08-25/26 [market-structure/99]. How much of the 98.7th-percentile speculative long and the 92nd-percentile hedger short survived that week is NOT PROVEN FROM AVAILABLE DATA. This is the single largest hole in this orb's read and is the reason the profile's freshness leg ('a current COMEX COT observation') fails independently of the missing vintage. It is also why no attempt is made anywhere in this orb to explain the price with positioning: ATTRIBUTION (MODULE_RULES 4a) - COMEX front-month copper +46.63% over 12 months (+US$2.11/lb to US$6.62/lb) [market-structure 02 section 1, TradingEconomics 2026-08-28, UNVINTAGED, that orb's fact not mine] times a sensitivity of price to managed-money net length: NO SUCH COEFFICIENT EXISTS IN THIS RUN = not computable, 0 US cents/lb of the +US$2.11/lb observed can be attributed to positioning -> 0% explained, 100% residual (unattributed). copper.comex-price-history is STRUCTURALLY ABSENT (no price-history connector exists for any commodity in the 27-connector registry), so no regression of price on positioning is possible and no published elasticity was retrieved. Any claim that speculative buying 'drove' this rally is unsupported and is not made.

EXPLICIT GAP ROW for required series copper.etf-flows, emitted so the absence is machine-visible. Zero strength, neutral, NON-VOTING - the etf-flows cluster casts no direction in this run. The USCF CPER issuer fund page was retrieved on 2026-08-28 and returned the field LABELS ('Shares Outstanding', 'Total Net Assets', 'NAV', 'Premium Discount') with NO POPULATED VALUES; the figures are rendered client-side and were not obtainable. The profile's source policy is 'lawful issuer publications only; otherwise unavailable', so third-party aggregator numbers CANNOT substitute - and in any case they contradict each other: AUM 'US$732m as of 2026-08-24' versus a separate description of '>US$760m in copper futures and an equal amount of cash collateral', plus a one-year flow figure of '+US$367.29m' [aggregator summaries retrieved 2026-08-28, unvintaged, not issuer publications]. Under CLAUDE.md section 4's conservative default none of these is adopted and no ETF flow direction is inferred; inferring a flow from price is explicitly forbidden. TWO FURTHER REASONS THIS ROW WOULD NOT VOTE EVEN IF RESOLVED: (1) CPER holds DEFERRED COMEX months - its August 2026 components included Dec-26 and May-27 - so a CPER creation is a bid for deferred copper, NOT confirmation of the front-month move [market-structure/01 section 2]; (2) CPER's own futures already sit INSIDE the 281,563 lots of COMEX open interest analysed under futures-positioning, so adding an ETF holdings number to a COT class total would DOUBLE-COUNT the same lots - that arithmetic is never performed anywhere in this orb. Miner-equity vehicles (COPX, ICOP, FCX) are deliberately excluded: the profile is explicit that miners are a levered confirmation, not the metal, and equity-fund flows are not copper flows.
